automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Only sources with a visible publication or update date inside this window qualify. Missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates are excluded.

federation_boundary.local_scope: AI-assisted development practice, including context architecture, guidance structure, agent operating practices, workflows, verification, governance, and local adoption patterns.
federation_boundary.upstream_scope: Broad AI ecosystem entities, including companies, models, products, developer tools, agentic frameworks, MCP servers, and general techniques.
federation_boundary.handling: Entity updates are recorded as upstream-owned. This artifact keeps only the downstream practice implication or routing note.

findings.source_title: AI Is Moving up the Software Lifecycle: From Code Review to PRD Governance
findings.summary: InfoQ reports that AI review is moving earlier in the development lifecycle, from code review into PRD validation, design inputs, and structured engineering artifact review.
findings.why_it_matters: The local wiki should treat AI-assisted development as a full lifecycle governance pattern, not only a code generation or code review practice.
findings.federation_note: Do not create local company pages. A future ingest pass can capture the local pattern of AI reviewing requirements and design artifacts before implementation.
follow_up_notes: Consider a downstream lens on lifecycle-level AI review gates if multiple raw sources converge.

findings.summary: Augment Code describes agent monitoring as trace-level telemetry over reasoning paths, tool calls, memory reads and writes, sub-agent handoffs, and state transitions because standard APM can miss semantic failures.
findings.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development practices need observability requirements for agent traces, not only build status, HTTP errors, or final outputs.
findings.federation_note: Keep Augment Code as upstream-owned product context. Local coverage should focus on trace and telemetry obligations for agent workflows.
follow_up_notes: Useful evidence for a practice page on agent observability and audit trails.

findings.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Tag in Slack beta for Enterprise and Team customers, emphasizing shared channel context, delegated tasks, permissioned channel access, and collaborative continuity.
findings.why_it_matters: Team-facing coding agents are moving into shared work channels, so local practice guidance needs boundaries for channel memory, permissions, task handoff, and visible progress threads.
findings.federation_note: The product launch belongs upstream. Local synthesis should cover practice implications for multiplayer agent context and permissioned workspace memory.
follow_up_notes: Watch for adoption examples showing how teams govern agents in shared communication channels.

findings.source_title: Changes to model selection for Free and Student plans
findings.summary: GitHub changed Copilot Free and Student plans so auto model selection is the default and only model selection experience, dynamically routing tasks across model families within plan restrictions.
findings.why_it_matters: Model routing is becoming a tool policy decision rather than a per-user choice, which affects reproducibility, auditability, and how coding-agent results are interpreted.
findings.federation_note: Keep Copilot product coverage upstream. Local practice implication is that model identity may be indirect and should be captured in evaluation and audit records when possible.
follow_up_notes: Potential ingest target for a local page on routing-aware evaluation records.

findings.source_title: Self-service credential revocation for incident response
findings.summary: GitHub added enterprise and self-service credential revocation flows for SSO authorizations, personal access tokens, SSH keys, and OAuth tokens, with audit logs and email notifications.
findings.why_it_matters: Agentic development increases the importance of rapid credential containment because coding agents can operate through developer tokens, SSH keys, OAuth grants, and connected tools.
findings.federation_note: Do not duplicate GitHub feature coverage. Local synthesis can use this as evidence for incident-response requirements around agent-accessible credentials.
follow_up_notes: Useful for a future governance page on break-glass credential response for coding-agent environments.

findings.source_title: Codex now offers pay-as-you-go pricing for teams
findings.summary: OpenAI updated an April Codex pricing announcement to say new Codex pay-as-you-go seats are no longer available for Business plans, while existing seats are unaffected.
findings.why_it_matters: Team adoption runbooks should avoid assuming that a previously available Codex seat or cost model remains available for new Business-plan users.
findings.federation_note: Pricing and product availability are upstream-owned. Local implication is adoption planning risk when automation budgets or team pilots depend on seat mechanics.
follow_up_notes: If ingested, keep this as a brief operating-model caveat rather than a product page.

findings.source_title: What nearly 10,000 developer environments reveal about agentic development risk
findings.summary: Snyk reports that AI coding tool sprawl, MCP servers, and agent skills are already measurable supply-chain layers in developer environments, with findings around MCP risk, prompt injection in tool descriptions, and malicious patterns in skills.
findings.why_it_matters: The local wiki should treat coding-agent configuration, skills, tool manifests, and MCP connections as governed development supply-chain inputs rather than incidental editor settings.
findings.federation_note: Keep Snyk and MCP broad coverage upstream. Local synthesis should focus on governance controls for agent configuration and instruction supply chains.
follow_up_notes: Strong candidate for a future ingest pass into governance and prompt-instruction supply-chain leaves.

findings.source_title: AI agent evaluation: frameworks and metrics that go beyond the benchmarks
findings.summary: Algolia frames agent evaluation as assessment of full execution trajectories, including tool calls, reasoning steps, execution order, performance, reliability, safety, governance, and human review loops.
findings.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development evals should assess trajectories and intermediate decisions, not only final code, final answers, or benchmark scores.
findings.federation_note: Do not create a local Algolia page. Use this only for local practice guidance on trajectory-level evals.
follow_up_notes: Pairs with agent observability sources for a durable eval-loop page.

findings.source_title: The Identity Problem Hiding in AI Agent Deployments
findings.summary: CrowdStrike argues that OAuth access tokens lack standard identity context for agent instance identity and the relationship between an agent and the user it represents.
findings.why_it_matters: Agent governance needs identity and audit records that distinguish the human requester, the agent instance, delegated authority, and downstream tool actions.
findings.federation_note: Standards and vendor background belong upstream. Local synthesis should capture agent identity as an audit and authorization practice requirement.
follow_up_notes: Potential evidence for a local governance leaf on agent identity and delegated authority.

findings.source_title: What Security Teams Should Require From an MCP Gateway
findings.summary: Barndoor describes MCP gateway controls for per-tool policy, per-user and per-group scoping, hosted tool catalog change detection, centralized audit logging, and data protection before tool responses reach a model.
findings.why_it_matters: MCP governance practice should be expressed as policy lifecycle, default-deny tool scoping, change review, and audit evidence rather than just whether a server is connected.
findings.federation_note: Keep vendor and protocol coverage upstream. Local synthesis should focus on control requirements for governed tool calls.
follow_up_notes: Could feed a downstream practice page on MCP policy and audit controls.

findings.source_title: Agentjacking: Your AI Coding Agent Can Be Hijacked
findings.summary: Digital Applied summarizes agentjacking as an attack pattern where malicious instructions hidden in externally controlled error data are retrieved through MCP and executed by a coding agent using legitimate credentials.
findings.why_it_matters: Coding-agent runbooks should treat tool output as untrusted data, gate shell execution, sandbox agents, and audit integrations that surface externally controlled content.
findings.federation_note: The attack class and affected products are upstream-owned. Local implication is runtime approval and trust-boundary practice for coding-agent tool output.
follow_up_notes: Primary Tenet disclosure is older than the cutoff, so use the June 24 synthesis only as a current practice-routing source.

findings.source_title: Long-horizon agent benchmarks are fragmenting: a field guide to what each one actually measures
findings.summary: Arize discusses fragmentation in long-horizon agent benchmarks and highlights that multi-step, tool-using agents require evaluation of the whole behavior trajectory, including incentives that can distort benchmark behavior.
findings.why_it_matters: Software engineering evals for coding agents should document what a benchmark measures, what incentives it creates, and whether it reflects local workflows, not just record leaderboard scores.
findings.federation_note: Benchmark entities belong upstream. Local synthesis should capture benchmark selection and interpretation practice for software engineering agents.
follow_up_notes: Good candidate for verification-and-evals ingest alongside Algolia and Augment monitoring sources.
